rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Taz subsection 1: it is chametz that has a permitted form; on erev Pesach after its prohibition time it is forbidden min b'mino in any amount because of davar sheyesh lo matirin.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: Magen Avraham subsection 2: forbidden substance exits from piece to piece without gravy — in my humble opinion this is wondrous, since if the entire matzah were chametz it would require against all of it because of infusion, and one cannot say that sixty against the edge that touches suffices, for from the other side the plain way through that edge is absorbed, which does not exit without gravy; if so what difference does it make that this side was not folded — nevertheless the taste of this matzah spreads through all of it; is the matzah a prophet that if all of it is chametz all spreads, and if this side is not chametz not all spreads — this is impossible to say.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/4:_: Magen Avraham subsection 4: what he wrote above that in chametz we do not find prohibition of sharpness, for even if they cooked in vinegar, nevertheless since chametz itself is not sharp it is like "the forbidden substance does not render forbidden" etc. — see there.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/5:_: Magen Avraham subsection 5: as proven in Tosafot beginning of Pesachim — only there; there one can say for the first reason regarding concern that one will come to eat from it they were stringent because they do not separate from it alone, as Tosafot wrote that one who vows taste permits for others and there is no karet in a vow, but in truth from nokshah it is proven because they do not separate from it alone; but regarding the law that in any amount, necessarily they were stringent only in combination with karet, for what he wrote that from chametz b'eyna there is no proof, for it is considered somewhat separating since it is the time of destruction — this is insufficient, for Rav who holds like R' Yehuda, chametz for afterward is d'oraisa, and nevertheless he said that in min b'mino in sixty yes, but in min b'mino in any amount like all prohibitions, for min b'mino in any amount; and if so for us also in min b'mino it is nullified like Rav in not its kind, and if so it is proven that without karet, even without separating alone, it is not in any amount.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/8:_: Unless the hand reaches yad soledes bo, since there is no gravy there; nevertheless even when Pesach enters, kli sheini does not require at least removal, for as soon as they removed it from the gravy with the wheat it became forbidden as removal; but if at the beginning of Pesach yad soledes bo, the entire thing is forbidden from the law of infusion.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/9:_: There in Darkei Moshe: but chametz that is in any amount is forbidden even in roasting; and at first glance this is difficult, for Shmuel said there is no difference except that it was cooked, but it was roasted and a peel was removed from it — and Shmuel holds min b'mino is not nullified, and if so it is proven even in any amount there is none; and even if one says he said so as explanation in the mishnah of the way, and this mishnah holds min b'mino is nullified, nevertheless why challenge on it from R' Hoshaya who said a kid roasted in its milk is forbidden etc. — perhaps R' Hoshaya holds like his teacher Rav that min b'mino is not nullified; and perhaps one can say Hagahot Maimoniyot holds milk and meat are called not its kind, not like Rashba and Ran; also one can say the any amount that spread outside of the removal spreads with the taste of the removal, and since the power of the permitted is mixed in it, it is called not its kind, as Ran wrote in perek Gid HaNasheh regarding once it gave taste in the piece; and only in chametz it is forbidden since also b'she'eino mino in any amount — according to this a dry thing, Hagahot Maimoniyot also agrees it is forbidden only as removal, and understand.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/12:_: And they give taste on Pesach — that it is not forbidden otherwise because of the crumbs themselves mixed in it, for which there would be a remedy to strain it now; but the difficulty for me is from Rama's language "however in a dry thing where there is concern" etc. — it is implied we come on it from the law of revival in dry; and so implied from what he wrote this law in that seif dealing with the law of revival; and if so at first glance even if one does not hold revival, behold the crumbs themselves were not nullified before Pesach, for one could clarify to remove the forbidden substance by straining — if so it is like crumbs fell into it now, which forbids in any amount, and this requires study.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] Chametz on Pesach forbids etc. By d'oraisa law chametz is like other prohibitions, but the Sages were stringent regarding it since it carries karet and one is not accustomed to separating from it throughout the year. Magen Avraham at the beginning of the siman, and Rambam chapter 15 of the Laws of Chametz siman 9 wrote the reason because it is a davar sheyesh lo matirin — see there, and Beit Yosef brought it. And Rama wrote in responsa siman 28: where there is an additional basis for leniency one may rely on what Mordechai wrote that there is basis to rely on his rulings and one may be lenient and nullify chametz in sixty like other prohibitions; and so in responsa Mishna Berurah siman 69, and also cited in Magen Avraham below siman 467 subsection 33; nevertheless in practice it appears from their words one does not rely on this unless there are many additional bases for leniency. Chok Yaakov sign 1, Chak Yosef sign 1, Makor Chayim sign 1, Chayei Adam general rule 121 sign 8.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) There. Whether in its own kind or not in its own kind etc. — meaning not in its own kind, where ordinarily in other prohibitions we follow taste; and in its own kind where in other prohibitions we estimate in sixty, as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 98 — see there; here regarding chametz there is no distinction and it forbids in any amount, even in benefit.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: (5) There. In any amount etc. — one explanation: rather less than sixty is called any amount; or in any amount that improved the mixture and it is sold for more than before — if so behold the Mechaber wrote below siman 467 seif 10 regarding a cooked chicken in which a split wheat was found on Pesach that it is permitted to sell it, and here he wrote that in any amount it forbids in benefit; rather certainly as we said. Peri Chadash. And Maamar Mordechai there sign 16 wrote that there he relied on Rosh that wheat even if split is not full chametz, therefore for benefit he relied to be lenient — see there; and see further in our words there in detail.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) There. In any amount etc., whether the substance of chametz dissolved or it is b'eyna and there is only its taste — it is in any amount. Rashba in responsa siman 30 and 53; and so it is explained from the Mechaber's words in this siman and siman 467. Peri Chadash. And so agreed Mateh Yehudah that also in taste alone it forbids in any amount — see there. And see above siman 442 sign 4; and regarding whether it is permitted to sell to a gentile outside the value of the forbidden substance in it, see below sign 13.
kaf-hachayyim/7:_: (7) There. In any amount etc., and even any amount of chametz nokshah which is forbidden rabbinically. Peri Chadash. And so Taz subsection 19: if chametz nokshah fell into food it is forbidden to eat on Pesach but permitted to retain after Pesach — see there. However Magen Avraham subsection 5 wrote in the name of Lekutim of Maharil that chametz nokshah even during Pesach is nullified in sixty since there is no karet, and he brought what Piskei Maharai siman 486 wrote that it forbids in any amount, and he challenged him and concluded that one who is lenient like Maharil does not lose — see there. And so agreed Nahar Shalom sign 2, Erech HaShulchan sign 9, Makor Chayim sign 7, Razah sign 8, Chok Yaakov. Chayei Adam general rule 121 sign 13. Magen Alef. However fruit juice with water, although it is nokshah, forbids in any amount. Makor Chayim there. And see below sign 268.
kaf-hachayyim/8:_: (8) There. In any amount etc., and if a prohibition forbidden in any amount became mixed in another dish — which is two any-amounts — Taz concludes in Yoreh De'ah siman 92 subsection 16: if a piece was forbidden in any amount and fell into another pot and they removed it, its discharge does not forbid in any amount, for we do not say two any-amounts; but wet in wet that became mixed this way is forbidden forever in any amount — see there. And so Peri Chadash agreed with Taz; and so Rabbi Akiva Eiger concludes sign 1 to be lenient regarding a piece forbidden in any amount that fell into another dish when there is majority against it and they recognize the piece and removed it; but if they do not recognize it, all is forbidden — see there. However Shach in Nekudat HaKesef there challenged Taz's words regarding permitting a piece forbidden in any amount that fell into another pot, and wrote that so all decisors practice to forbid all mixtures — see there. And so agreed Erech HaShulchan in this siman sign 1 and wrote and not like Taz — see there. And so Magen Avraham in siman 467 subsection 13. Chok Yaakov in this siman sign 5 and siman 467 sign 27. Chak Yosef sign 6, Mateh Yehudah, and wrote that so is proven from Mechaber and Rama's words, and such is the custom in the city of Algezaid — see there. Razah sign 16. Chayei Adam general rule 121 sign 8. However in a doubt of rabbinic prohibition in any amount, Rav Beit Yehudah page 109 wrote a mixture of two is permitted, and so he agreed — see there. And so Rav Beit Din siman 563: if there is doubt that none of the chametz entered mixture B but all chametz remained in mixture A, according to all it is permitted — see there. And Beit Din Erech HaShulchan sign 4; however he wrote that from Magen Avraham's words subsection 26 it is implied that even if there is doubt perhaps the chametz remained in mixture A, we forbid — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/10:_: (10) One who cooked fish in a chametz pan that was not used for many days, and the spoon with which he stirred later stirred another dish, and from it they gave some to another dish — see in Shevut Yaakov part 1 siman 21 who wrote one may not be lenient in this (and this is according to Rama's view below seif 10 that he forbids taste for detriment on Pesach — see there), unless there is otherwise basis to permit; and here there is additional basis to permit taste for detriment even on Pesach b'dieved after two months (and it is implied that also what was cooked in the pan is permitted b'dieved), on condition it is folded so that what is cooked in it is not a sharp thing (see Yoreh De'ah siman 93 in the gloss and siman 122 seif 3 in the gloss); and from this one learns to be stringent in covering a pot even though it is not ben yomo, nevertheless after two months there is room to permit; however l'chatchila in all prohibitions it is forbidden to use vessels that are not ben yomo without hagalah even if not used for many years, and all the more chametz — see there. And Beit Din Shaarei Tzedek sign 2; however in responsa Chacham Tzvi siman 75 he wrote to permit specifically if twelve hours passed after chametz was cooked in it, and Rav Naftali Cohen agreed with him as written there siman 76, and likewise siman 80 — see there. And this will be explained further below siman 451 sign 4 — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/11:_: (11) A loaf of the homeowner's chametz that became mixed among loaves of matzah — even if it mixed in a thousand, all are forbidden in eating and benefit because it is a davar sheb'minyan (as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 110); and it appears to me that even after Pesach they are forbidden; and if the bread was cut or broken it is permitted after Pesach. And there are those who say after Pesach it is permitted (meaning even if still whole), for they permitted all chametz mixtures after Pesach even though its prohibition is in any amount, and a davar sheb'minyan should not be more stringent than them whose prohibition is in any amount; and in this I am stringent, for they made a mixture of davar sheb'minyan like the body of the prohibition itself. Sefer Beit Moed. Berakh Yaakov sign 2, and so Peri Chadash in siman 448 seif 3 to forbid also after Pesach — see there; and see below seif 9 and in our words there in detail.
